stem: In which direction do signals travel on the address bus?

options.content: One way, from the processor to memory
options.rationale: Correct: addresses are only sent by the processor.

options.content: One way, from memory to the processor
options.rationale: Memory never sends addresses to the processor on this bus.

options.content: Both ways, as for the data bus
options.rationale: The data bus is two-way; the address bus is not.

options.content: Both ways, depending on the clock
options.rationale: The clock does not change the direction of the address bus.

explanation: The address bus is one-way: the processor chooses the location.

stem: Which bus carries the memory read, memory write, clock and interrupt signals?

options.content: The control bus
options.rationale: Correct: it carries signals that co-ordinate the components.

options.content: The address bus
options.rationale: The address bus carries only the address of a location.

options.content: The data bus
options.rationale: The data bus carries data and instructions.

options.content: The serial bus
options.rationale: A serial bus is a different kind of connection, not one of the three internal buses.

explanation: Control bus: read, write, clock, interrupt request, reset and similar signals.

stem: What happens to the number of memory locations that can be addressed when one more wire is added to the address bus?

options.content: It increases by one location
options.rationale: Each wire doubles the combinations, it does not add just one.

options.content: It stays the same because the data bus decides it
options.rationale: The data bus width does not decide the number of locations.

options.content: It doubles
options.rationale: Correct: each extra wire doubles the number of different addresses.

options.content: It is halved because each address is longer
options.rationale: A longer address allows more locations, not fewer.

explanation: With n wires there are 2^n addresses, so n + 1 wires give 2 × 2^n.

stem: Which port carries both digital video and digital audio in one cable?

options.content: VGA
options.rationale: VGA carries analogue video only.

options.content: HDMI
options.rationale: Correct: High-Definition Multimedia Interface carries both.

options.content: A serial port for a mouse
options.rationale: This is not a video port.

options.content: An Ethernet port
options.rationale: Ethernet is used for network cabling, not for sending video to a screen.

explanation: HDMI carries digital pictures and sound together.

stem: Why can a picture sent through a long VGA cable look less sharp than the same picture sent through HDMI?

options.content: VGA sends the picture in fewer colours than HDMI always does
options.rationale: The number of colours is not what makes a long cable look soft.

options.content: VGA is a digital signal that is lost when the cable is long
options.rationale: VGA is analogue, not digital.

options.content: VGA uses the address bus to send the picture
options.rationale: The video cable is not part of the address bus.

options.content: VGA is an analogue signal, which picks up noise
options.rationale: Correct: analogue signals vary continuously and are affected by interference.

explanation: A digital signal is either 0 or 1 and can be recovered; an analogue signal varies continuously and picks up noise along the cable.
hints: Which of the two ports is digital end to end?

stem: A computer has a 16-bit address bus and each address refers to one byte. What is the greatest amount of memory it can address?

options.content: 16 KiB
options.rationale: 16 KiB would need 14 address lines.

options.content: 256 KiB
options.rationale: 256 KiB needs 18 address lines.

options.content: 64 KiB
options.rationale: Correct: 2^16 = 65 536 bytes.

options.content: 16 MiB
options.rationale: 16 MiB needs 24 address lines.

explanation: 2^16 = 65 536 locations = 64 KiB.

stem: A new processor has a 128-bit data bus where the old one had a 64-bit data bus, with the same number of transfers per second. What is the effect?

options.content: Twice as many memory locations can be addressed
options.rationale: The number of locations depends on the address bus.

options.content: Twice as many bits are moved in each second
options.rationale: Correct: each transfer carries twice as much data.

options.content: The memory becomes non-volatile
options.rationale: Volatility is a property of the memory type.

options.content: The control bus is no longer needed
options.rationale: The control bus is still needed for signals.

explanation: Data rate = width × transfers per second, so doubling the width doubles the data moved.
hints: Which bus decides how much data moves in a transfer?

stem: A technician says a classroom projector only has a VGA socket, but the teacher's laptop has HDMI only and sound must also reach the speakers. Which statement is correct?

options.content: No adapter is needed because both carry the same signal
options.rationale: HDMI is digital and VGA analogue, so an adapter is needed.

options.content: The sound will pass through the VGA socket as well
options.rationale: VGA does not carry audio.

options.content: HDMI cannot be converted to any other type of signal
options.rationale: Adapters that convert HDMI to VGA exist.

options.content: An adapter is needed and sound needs its own cable
options.rationale: Correct: VGA is analogue and carries no audio.

explanation: VGA carries analogue video only, so a converter and a separate audio connection are needed.
hints: Which signal is digital and which carries sound?

stem: The data bus is a one-way bus from memory to the processor.
explanation: False. The data bus is two-way: data goes to the processor on a read and from the processor to memory on a write.

stem: A wider address bus allows a larger number of memory locations to be addressed.
explanation: True. n address lines give 2^n locations, so more lines mean more addressable locations.

stem: Match each bus or port to what it carries.

right.content: Read, write, clock and interrupt signals
Serial data and a small amount of power
The address of a memory location
Data and instructions, in both directions

explanation: Each bus or port has one main kind of signal.

stem: Complete the steps of a memory read.

payload.template: The address is placed on the {{blank:a}} bus and the {{blank:b}} line of the control bus is activated. The contents of the location travel back on the {{blank:c}} bus and arrive in the memory data register.

explanation: Address bus, read line, data bus.

stem: How many different addresses can be made with a 12-wire address bus?
explanation: 2^12 = 4096 addresses.

stem: A small controller has 6 KiB of memory with one byte per location. What is the smallest number of address lines that can address every location?
workedSolution:
1. 6 KiB = 6 × 1024 = 6144 locations.
2. 2^12 = 4096 is too small.
3. 2^13 = 8192 is enough, so 13 lines are needed.
hints: 6 KiB = 6144 locations; find the smallest n with 2^n at least that big.

stem: A processor has a 28-line address bus and each address refers to one byte. What is the maximum memory it can address, in MiB?
A processor with a 32-bit data bus copies a block of 128 bytes from memory. How many transfers on the data bus are needed?
explanation: 1024 bits at 32 bits per transfer is 32 transfers.
workedSolution:
1. 128 bytes = 128 × 8 = 1024 bits.
2. Each transfer carries 32 bits.
3. 1024 ÷ 32 = 32 transfers.
hints: Bits to move = bytes × 8; divide by the width.

stem: A 64-bit data bus makes 25 million transfers per second. Calculate the data rate in megabits per second (Mbit/s).
hints: Data rate = width × transfers per second.

stem: Describe how the processor reads an instruction from memory using the three buses. [4]

points.description: The address of the instruction is copied from the MAR onto the address bus
A memory read signal is sent along the control bus
The contents of the addressed location are placed on the data bus by the memory
The instruction travels along the data bus into the MDR

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The address goes from the MAR onto the address bus. The control bus carries a read signal. The memory places the instruction on the data bus and it arrives in the MDR.

explanation: Each bus is used once, in order.
hints: Four steps: address, read signal, data back, MDR.

stem: Compare an HDMI connection with a VGA connection for a school projector. [3]

points.description: HDMI carries a digital signal whereas VGA carries an analogue signal
HDMI carries sound as well as video; VGA carries video only
The HDMI picture is not degraded by noise on the cable / VGA can lose sharpness

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: HDMI is digital and also carries sound, while VGA is analogue and carries only video. A digital picture is not affected by noise, so it stays sharp, but a VGA picture can lose sharpness.

explanation: Digital against analogue, audio, quality.
hints: Compare signal type, sound and quality.

stem: Explain why the address bus only needs to carry signals in one direction. [2]

points.description: The processor always decides which location is to be read or written
Memory and devices only respond to the address; they never send an address back

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The processor decides which location it wants, so the address always travels from the processor to the memory. Memory never needs to send an address to the processor.

explanation: The processor always initiates the access.

stem: A microcontroller for a weather station in Kariba has an 18-line address bus and an 8-bit data bus. Each memory location holds 8 bits.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of memory locations that can be addressed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the memory capacity in KiB.
parts.workedSolution:
1. 8 bits = 1 byte per location.
2. Bytes = 262 144.
3. 262 144 ÷ 1024 = 256 KiB.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: A 32-bit word is read from memory. How many transfers on the data bus are needed?

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State the number of locations if three more address lines are added.

points.description: Each extra line doubles the number, so it is multiplied by 8

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each extra line doubles the number, so three lines multiply it by eight, to 2^21 = 2 097 152 locations.

explanation: An 18-line address bus gives 2^18 = 262 144 locations (256 KiB); an 8-bit data bus needs 4 transfers per 32-bit word; three more lines give 2^21 locations.
hints: Bits to move ÷ bus width = transfers.

stem: A teacher at a school in Gweru connects a laptop to a projector, a printer and a flash drive.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which port can supply a small amount of power to a connected flash drive?

options.content: VGA
options.rationale: VGA only carries video.

options.content: The address bus
options.rationale: This is inside the computer.

options.content: Audio out
options.rationale: This outputs an analogue sound signal, not power for a device.

options.content: USB
options.rationale: Correct.

parts.explanation: USB carries data and a small amount of power.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain what is meant by hot-plugging and why it is useful.

points.description: A device can be connected or disconnected while the computer is switched on
The user need not shut down and restart the computer

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Hot-plugging means connecting a device while the computer is on. It saves the user from shutting down and restarting.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The projector has an HDMI input. State three advantages of using HDMI rather than VGA for this connection.

points.description: Carries sound as well as video
Digital signal, so the picture is not degraded by noise
A single cable and connector is needed for sound and picture

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: HDMI carries sound and vision, the digital signal gives a sharper picture, and only one cable is needed.

explanation: HDMI digital video and audio; VGA analogue video; USB serial data and power, hot-pluggable.
hints: Match each port to the signal it carries.
